warum.title: Why Context Fit?
warum.p1: We all want to get fit, but sometimes life gets in the way and it's hard to know where to start. Don't worry, I'll take care of that. Together we build a plan made just for you, including a training program, nutrition guidance and changes to your lifestyle. Everything is designed to fit your individual situation. The plan is built around your context, hence the name: Context Fit.
warum.p2: Context Fit: the right place for busy people and grappling athletes. As a black belt in BJJ and Luta Livre and a dedicated strength athlete, I especially care about helping other grapplers get into their best possible grappling shape.

grapplingTraining.title: Grappling Training
grapplingTraining.tagline: Reach your full potential on the mat
grapplingTraining.body: Years of experience in BJJ, MMA and strength & conditioning.

bio.p1: My name is Bram van Koppen, and sport has been a fixed part of my life since I was young. I started out in karate and later discovered Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu, which is still my biggest passion today. Over time I realized I had to get stronger to reach my full potential. That's how strength training found its place in my routine. From Olympic weightlifting to powerlifting and other disciplines, I've explored a lot of paths to develop as an athlete and as a coach.
bio.p2: Alongside my work as a coach, I'm also a qualified physiotherapist. That lets me combine better performance with injury prevention and rehabilitation.
bio.p3: I'm the proud father of two children. That's exactly what taught me how important effective, realistic training methods are. Balancing family, work and training is a challenge, and that's why I focus on making fitness a practical, sustainable part of my clients' everyday lives.

comeback.title: My comeback
comeback.p1: About two years ago, I had to admit something to myself. I wasn't in the shape I thought I was. I weighed 104 kg, even though I trained regularly. I had been fooling myself.
comeback.p2: The first step was <hl>radical honesty</hl>. No excuses. I found three things: I had massively underestimated my calorie intake. Despite training on the mat, I was too inactive in everyday life, and I wasn't getting enough sleep. Not easy with two small children, but I had also been making it too easy on myself.
comeback.p3: So I changed it: more movement during the day, tracking calories, preparing meals, following a structured training plan consistently and, most importantly: <hl>sticking with it every single day</hl>.
comeback.p4: The result: from 104 kg down to 88 kg. More energy and more self-confidence.
comeback.p5: Simple doesn't mean easy. <hl>Consistency</hl> was what really made the difference. I know how hard it is to balance family, work and your own health. That's exactly why I help you find the approach that fits your life.

Rechner.intro: Your job and your steps are one thing. Training comes on top. Not sure about your PAL? Pick the lower level.

koerperfettReferenz.caption: Estimate roughly where you stand — it doesn't need to be exact.

zielBeschreibung.maintain: Keep your weight, improve strength and shape.
zielBeschreibung.deficit: Lose fat, keep as much muscle as possible.
zielBeschreibung.bulk: Build muscle with a controlled surplus.

palHelper.sedentary: Office job, few steps. Sitting for most of the day.
palHelper.lightly_active: Some walking, light work on your feet. No physical job.
palHelper.active: On your feet a lot. Lots of steps, not “I train 6×”.
palHelper.very_active: Physical job or a very high step count. Still without the gym or the mat.

Rechner.palDauerhinweis: PAL is only about your daily life. Don't pick “very active” because you train. Training minutes are added on top. Not sure? Go one level lower.

warnungen.negativeKohlenhydrate: The deficit is tough on rest days. Protein and fat take up almost everything. Either almost no carbs on rest days — or the deficit is too big.
warnungen.koerperfettUnrealistisch: Katch-McArdle needs a body fat number. Entering 25% “because it sounds about right” throws off your BMR.
warnungen.tageMismatch: Sessions and rest days should add up to 7 — right now it's {total}.

Rechner.footer: An estimate, not medical advice. A proper measurement beats guessing.
